claims.text: The wear performance of HEA protective coatings is primarily governed by their density of lattice distortions.
A multi-element solid solution produces high lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion during sliding wear.
Impeded dislocation motion enhances resistance to plastic deformation during sliding wear.
The initial sputter-deposited coating is a single-phase random multi-element solid solution.
The initial coating has high configurational entropy and high lattice distortion.
Replacing principal elements with an element of similar atomic radius but lower mixing enthalpy will reduce lattice strain and configurational disorder.
Atomic-scale lattice distortions act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Multiple unsynchronized atomic sizes cause severe lattice distortion in HEAs.
Hindering dislocation glide enhances the coating's ability to absorb and dissipate mechanical energy.
Enhanced mechanical-energy absorption and dissipation improve wear resistance.
Lowering lattice distortion will increase wear rate.
The modified coating with reduced lattice distortion will have greater wear volume than the baseline coating.
The modified coating will show more pronounced wear artifacts and material removal than the baseline coating.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold for stable, single-phase HEA solid-solution coatings under ordinary sliding-wear conditions below severe-plastic-deformation thresholds.
The proposed relationship is not expected to apply when additional wear mechanisms, such as oxidation-driven high-temperature wear, become active.
Nanograin boundaries may also contribute to the wear performance of HEA coatings.
Wear performance statistically indistinguishable from or better than the baseline in the reduced-distortion coating would falsify the proposed governing role of lattice distortion.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes replacing one or more principal elements, which need not reduce the number of components, whereas the mechanism later characterizes the intervention as lowering compositional complexity.
